note: One profile per town on the Peninsula, written from what is on the site. The city side is not done yet. `minutesFromHome` is recomputed from wherever you are.

items.name: Palo Alto
items.famousFor: Stanford, the HP Garage, and the downtown Silicon Valley grew up around
items.cafe: Goodthing on Ramona — the upstairs loft, and the Einspänner
items.bakery: Mademoiselle Colette on Lytton — the almond croissant
items.culture: The Cantor and the Rodin garden at Stanford — both free
items.park: Gamble Garden, two and a half acres off Waverley, free and rarely busy
items.unusual: The HP Garage on Addison Avenue, the birthplace of Silicon Valley, seen from the sidewalk
items.food: The Saturday farmers’ market on Gilman Street, there since 1983
items.walk: Ramona Street → University Avenue → Addison Avenue for the HP Garage
items.hidden: The Baylands boardwalk at dawn, a quarter of a mile over the marsh to open water

items.name: Menlo Park
items.famousFor: Kepler's Books and the Santa Cruz Avenue high street
items.cafe: Café Borrone, next door to Kepler's since 1989
items.bakery: Mademoiselle Colette on Santa Cruz Avenue
items.culture: Kepler's — the Peninsula's counterculture bookshop since 1955, with a serious events programme

items.name: Mountain View
items.famousFor: Castro Street and the Computer History Museum
items.culture: The Computer History Museum on Shoreline Boulevard
items.park: Shoreline Park — the lake, and the bay trail out over the marshes

items.name: Los Altos
items.famousFor: A small-town Main Street, a few minutes from everything that is not
items.culture: Linden Tree Books, the children's bookshop on State Street
items.food: Chef Chu's, open since 1970 on San Antonio Road
